answer: One defense is a bonded reputation ledger: each agent locks a refundable stake before it can trade, and every completed job adds a small, non-transferable reputation credit. A Sybil attacker who spins up thousands of fresh identities starts at the nadir of trust, so counterparties only offer tiny, low-value tasks. To reach the pearl tier of high-value work, an identity must accumulate a long history of successful deliveries, like an ember slowly building heat. Faking that history costs real stake and months of honest work per identity, so mass forgery becomes uneconomical.
